subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Earl Grey and Bergamot
description: A fast breakdown of Earl Grey and Bergamot for builders.

hook.text: Earl Grey is black tea scented with oil of bergamot—a citrus fruit that looks like a lumpy lemon.

buildup.text: Bergamot grows almost exclusively in Calabria, Italy. Its oil is also the top note in many perfumes.

discovery.text: The blend is named after Charles Grey, British Prime Minister in the 1830s, though the origin story varies.

twist.text: Lady Grey tea was created by Twinings in 1994 as a milder, more citrus-forward version for people who find Earl Grey too strong.

climax.text: Earl Grey is now one of the world's best-known flavored teas, sold in over 100 countries.

punchline.text: Black tea, Italian citrus, British name. A global classic.

quiz.question: What gives Earl Grey its distinctive flavor?

details.summary: Earl Grey is a black tea flavored with oil of bergamot, a citrus fruit from southern Italy. Named after the 19th-century British Prime Minister, its distinctive floral-citrus aroma has made it one of the world's most recognizable tea blends and a cornerstone of British tea culture.
details.whyItMatters: Earl Grey bridges pure tea tradition and flavored blending. Its global popularity shows how a simple addition can create an entirely new tea identity.
takeaways: Earl Grey is black tea scented with bergamot citrus oil
It is named after a 19th-century British Prime Minister
Quality varies enormously by tea base and bergamot source

faq.question: What is bergamot and where does it come from?
faq.answer: Bergamot is a small citrus fruit, Citrus bergamia, grown mainly in Calabria, Italy. Its aromatic rind yields an essential oil with floral and citrus notes. About 80 percent of the world's bergamot comes from a small coastal region in southern Italy.

faq.question: What makes a good Earl Grey versus a bad one?
faq.answer: Quality depends on the base tea and bergamot oil. Premium versions use whole-leaf black tea and natural bergamot oil from Calabria. Cheap Earl Greys use dust-grade tea and synthetic bergamot flavoring that tastes harsh and artificial. The difference is immediately noticeable.
